FOOTNOTES

1/ The operating lump sum appropriation includes \$776,600 from the water quality fee fund established by section 49-210, Arizona Revised Statutes, FOR to add two FTE positions to process an increase in permit applications resulting from revised aquifer water quality standards. The department of environmental quality may only spend these monies if matching amounts of aquifer protection permit program fees collected pursuant to section 49-241.02, Arizona Revised Statutes, are deposited in the water quality fee fund established by section 49-210, Arizona Revised Statutes, by the end of fiscal year 2026-2027. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

2/ A.R.S. § 49-282 as limited by the Environment Budget Reconciliation Bill requires an annual \$15,000,000 transfer from the Corporate Income Tax to the Water Quality Assurance Revolving Fund. Although the transfer is not included in the annual General Appropriations Act, it is shown here as a General Fund expenditure. The Corporate Income Tax transfer was suspended for FY 2026. The 2027 Baseline restores the annual transfer.

FOOTNOTES

3/ The department of environmental quality shall report annually on the progress of WQARF activities, including emergency response, priority site remediation, cost recovery activity, revenue and expenditure activity and other WQARF-funded program activity. The department shall submit the fiscal year 2026-2027 report to the joint legislative budget committee on or before September 1, 2026. This report shall also include a budget for the WQARF program that is developed in consultation with the WQARF advisory board. This budget shall specify the monies budgeted for each listed site during fiscal year 2026-2027. In addition, the department and the WQARF advisory board shall prepare and submit to the joint legislative budget committee, on or before October 1, 2026, a report in a table format summarizing the current progress on remediation of each listed site on the WQARF registry. The table shall include the stage of remediation for each site at the end of fiscal year 2025-2026, indicate whether the current stage of remediation is anticipated to be completed in fiscal year 2026-2027 and indicate the anticipated stage of remediation at each listed site at the end of fiscal year 2026- 2027, assuming fiscal year 2026-2027 funding levels. The department and the WQARF advisory board may include other relevant information about the listed sites in the table. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

4/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.   
5/ All monies in the department of environmental quality indirect cost fund established by section 49-115, Arizona Revised Statutes, including the beginning balance, that are in excess of \$19,603,200 in fiscal year 2026-2027 are appropriated to the department. Before spending indirect cost fund monies in excess of \$19,603,200 in fiscal year 2026-2027, the department shall report the intended use of the monies to the joint legislative budget committee. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

FOOTNOTES

6/ All permit administration fund monies received by the department of environmental quality in excess of \$7,165,200 in fiscal year 2026-2027 are appropriated to the department. Before spending permit administration fund monies in excess of \$7,165,200 in fiscal year 2026-2027, the department shall report the intended use of the monies to the joint legislative budget committee. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$69,937,300 and 360.7 FTE Positions in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts consist of:

Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Air Quality Support

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,170,100) from the Air Quality Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding of air quality initiatives, including a state match for a Diesel Emissions Reduction Act grant and additional support for federal Clean Air Act requirements.

Emissions Control Contractor Payment

The Baseline includes \$28,894,500 from the Emissions Inspection Fund in FY 2027 for Emissions Control Contractor Payment. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The Emissions Control Program is operated by a contractor in the Phoenix Metropolitan Area and the Tucson Metropolitan Area with the purpose of identifying polluting motor vehicles. The program is funded through test fees that are charged to motorists. Statute does not specify a fee level.

As session law, the Baseline would maintain emission inspection fees in FY 2027 for Area A at the June 30, 2025, Area A fee level. The FY 2026 Environment Budget Reconciliation Bill (BRB) included a provision requiring ADEQ to maintain emission inspection fees in FY 2026 for Area A at the June 30, 2025, Area A fee level. The FY 2025 Environment BRB required ADEQ to reduce emissions inspection fees for Area A such that total Area A collections were reduced by 5% of the level of FY 2024 Area A fee collections. Area A refers to the Phoenix Metropolitan Area and includes Maricopa County as well as portions of Pinal and Yavapai Counties.

As of November 30, 2025, both Phoenix Metropolitan Area and Tucson Metropolitan area vehicle owners pay \$16.15 for the onboard diagnostic test (previously \$17.00 in the Phoenix area and \$12.25 in the Tucson area.)

Zero-Emission Heavy-Duty Eight-Ton Pilot Program

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a Zero-Emission Heavy-Duty Eight-Ton Pilot Program. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2025 budget appropriated \$1,000,000 from the General Fund on a one-time basis for ADEQ to implement a pilot program to replace diesel heavy duty trucks with zero-emission vehicles. ADEQ did not report any expenditures in FY 2025. An FY 2026 budget footnote extended the appropriation lapse date through FY 2026.

WQARF Priority Site Remediation

The Baseline includes \$15,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Water Quality Assurance Revolving Fund (WQARF) Priority Site Remediation. Adjustments are as follows:

WQARF Fund Shift

The Baseline includes an increase of \$15,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 and a corresponding decrease of \$(15,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund to remove a one-time fund shift. (For information on the deposit, please see the WQARF Deposit line item.)

A.R.S. § 49-282 requires WQARF to be funded from an annual \$15,000,000 transfer from the Corporate Income Tax (CIT). In addition, WQARF generates other revenue from various license and registration fees. A.R.S. § 49-282 directs the State Treasurer to adjust the \$15,000,000 CIT transfer so that, when combined with the WQARF feegenerated revenue, the program receives \$18,000,000 annually.

The Baseline would restore an Environment BRB provision notwithstanding the \$18,000,000 annual funding level for WQARF and limiting the General Fund transfer to \$15,000,000.

The FY 2026 Environment BRB suspended A.R.S. § 49-282 to eliminate the use of General Fund for WQARF in FY 2026. In FY 2025, the WQARF program received \$15,000,000 from the General Fund and \$2,261,400 from fee revenues pursuant to A.R.S. § 49-288 for a total of \$17,261,400. (For information on the deposit, please see the WQARF Deposit line item.)

Background – The WQARF program is similar to the federal Superfund program in that it is designed to monitor and remediate contaminated groundwater at specified sites. Program expenditures include searching for responsible polluters, conducting risk assessments and remediation feasibility studies, and contracting for remediation services.

WQARF Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a WQARF deposit. Adjustments are as follows:

WQARF Fund Shift

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(15,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund in FY 2027 and a corresponding increase of \$15,000,000 from the General Fund to remove a one-time fund shift. (Please see the WQARF Priority Site Remediation line item for more information.)

Iron King Mine – Humboldt Smelter Cleanup

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Iron King Mine – Humboldt Smelter Cleanup. Adjustments are as follows:

text:
Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(2,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for the first installment of the state's share of cleanup for the Iron King Mine and Humboldt Smelter Superfund site.

ADEQ signed a Superfund State Contract with the federal Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 2023 to begin cleanup of the site, with the state responsible for 10% of total cleanup costs, or \$8.3 million. Per the contract, the state is required to pay at least \$2 million every 12 months. The EPA first listed the former Iron King Mine and Humboldt Smelter site on the Superfund National Priorities List in 2008.

Safe Drinking Water Program

The Baseline includes \$2,027,700 from the Safe Drinking Water Program Fund in FY 2027 for the Safe Drinking Water Program. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The Safe Drinking Water Program Fund receives the first \$1,800,000 of Public Water System (PWS) tax revenues.

Water Quality Fee Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a Water Quality Fee Fund Deposit. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(9,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund in FY 2027 to remove a one-time deposit into the Water Quality Fee Fund (WQFF) to address a funding shortfall.

This line item only reflects the transfer of revenue into the WQFF. The actual expenditure of any monies from the WQFF is displayed as part of the ADEQ operating budget. The FY 2025 budget made a one-time transfer of \$7,200,000 from the Air Quality Fund to the WQFF to address a funding shortfall. (Please see the ADEQ narrative in the FY 2026 Appropriations Report and FY 2026 Baseline for background on prior deposits to this fund and adjustments to the WQFF appropriation authority since FY 2023.)

The Baseline would:

As session law, continue to allow the department to utilize up to \$6,531,000 from the Underground Storage Tank (UST) Revolving Fund in FY 2027 for department administrative expenses and for sewage remediation.

As session law, restore a provision notwithstanding the \$18,000,000 annual funding level for the Water Quality Assurance Revolving Fund (WQARF) and limiting the General Fund transfer to \$15,000,000. The FY 2026 budget suspended statute to eliminate the use of the General Fund for WQARF in FY 2026.

As session law, maintain emission inspection fees in FY 2027 for Area A at the June 30, 2025, Area A fee level. Area A refers to the Phoenix Metropolitan Area and includes Maricopa County as well as portions of Pinal and Yavapai Counties.

PFAS Mitigation

The FY 2024 budget appropriated \$5,000,000 from the General Fund for PFAS Mitigation. This appropriation is non-lapsing.

PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) are long-lasting synthetic chemicals that are frequently used in industrial and consumer products, including non-stick cookware, certain firefighting foams, and water-resistant apparel. Because they are resistant to environmental breakdown, these chemicals often leak into soil, water, and air. Studies have shown that exposure to PFAs can result in a range of health risks for both humans and wildlife, including but not limited to cancer and reproductive harm.

Pursuant to a FY 2024 budget footnote requiring an update by July 21, 2024, ADEQ reported allocating \$2,469,000 for mitigation projects; \$1,131,000 for PFAS sampling to identify and monitor sites; \$1,000,000 for hydrogeologic studies to support rural water providers; and \$400,000 for other expenses, including preparing materials for water professionals about PFAS detection and mitigation and additional sampling of systems with significant PFAS contamination. In FY 2025, the department expended \$3,409,200 of the appropriation.

Underground Storage Tank Program

ADEQ is responsible for compliance with federal and state regulation for underground storage tanks and systems that store regulated substances like petroleum.

Laws 2025, Chapter 77 required ADEQ submit an annual report on the underground storage tank approval process to the Joint Legislative Budget Committee, Senate President, and Speaker of the House of Representatives starting on September 1, 2025.

According to the latest report, 91 facilities participated in the program in FY 2025, with \$20,168,800 in preapproved funding. Of that amount, ADEQ has reimbursed \$6,508,000. The remaining \$13,660,800 has yet to be distributed.

Source of Revenue: Legislative appropriations and fees received from water quality regulatory programs, including fees for technical review of Aquifer Protection Permits (APP), reclaimed water permits and Arizona Discharge Elimination System (AZDPES) permits, engineering reviews of drinking water facilities, wastewater and sewage collection systems, and the review and certification of potable water systems, sewage treatment plants and their operating personnel, and to establish a permit for direct potable reuse of treated wastewater. Revenues also come from annual fees paid by APP and AZDPES permittees.

Purpose of Fund: To pay the costs of water quality programs. The fund is exempt from A.R.S. § 35-190, relating to lapsing of appropriations.
